meta.title: Mia's Talk about the Sun Bear
meta.textType: dialogue: a short talk with facts

paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, the Explorers sat in a circle in the school library. Mia stood in front of them with a big picture of a bear. Leo wore sunglasses and a serious face, because he was the reporter that day. "Mia will give a short talk," said Teacher Kim. "After the talk, you will have a small test with three questions." "Will it be hard?" asked May. "No, just listen well," said Teacher Kim.

"Today I will talk about the sun bear," said Mia. "I discovered it in a book at the town library last month." "The sun bear is the smallest bear in the world." "It is about one meter long." "It has a golden mark on its chest, and the mark looks like the rising sun." "That is the reason for its name."

"Sun bears live in forests in Southeast Asia, including Thailand," said Mia. "They need a large area of forest, because they walk a long way to find food." "They eat fruit, insects, and honey." "A sun bear has a very long tongue, about twenty centimeters." "It uses its tongue to take honey from a nest in a tree." "Twenty centimeters?" said Leo. "That is longer than my pencil!"

"What does 'tongue' mean?" asked May. Lily opened the dictionary on the table. "It says, 'The soft part in your mouth that you use to taste food,'" she read. "Thank you," said May, and she smiled at Leo. Leo laughed and took off his sunglasses. "Mia, why do you like this bear?" he asked as a reporter. "It is small, but it is brave and clever," said Mia.

"Now it is time for the test," said Teacher Kim. "Question one: what is the smallest bear in the world?" "The sun bear!" said all the children. "Question two: how long is its tongue?" "About twenty centimeters," said Leo, and he smiled. "Question three: where does the sun bear live?" "In the forests of Southeast Asia," said May and Lily together. "Three out of three," said Teacher Kim. "Thank you, Mia."
